project_folder: CD Prabhakar Reddy Project Id B83CC285

verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 7 and 9 (Site-Exterior view, Site Layout - Top View, Proposed PV Area) all show a fixed-tilt PV array installed directly on open farmland/soil, with no building or roof structure anywhere in frame.
verdicts.rationale: No roof is visible in any site photo; the array is clearly ground-mounted on farmland, consistent with 'Other / Ground-mounted system'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6 exterior views and page 9 PV-area photo show open, mostly flat farmland with only sparse low scrub and a few scattered utility poles well outside the array footprint; no trees, tanks or walls sit over the panel area.
verdicts.rationale: No obstruction is visible over the array in any photo, consistent with the 'No' answer, though the field extends beyond the frame in some shots.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 CAD layout drawing 'Lepakshi Farm Land - 35.67 kWp' has a note box stating 'Panels Slope: 10 Degrees'; page 6/9 photos show a shallow, low-profile fixed-tilt array consistent with a small tilt angle.
verdicts.rationale: The layout drawing explicitly states a 10-degree panel slope, matching the designer's answer, and the photographed tilt looks visually shallow/consistent with 10°.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.designer_notes: EcoSoch Ground mounted (Ground Mount HDGI with Galvalume)
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 layout drawing note box states 'Type of Structure: EcoSoch Ground mounted', and pages 6/9 photos show a ground-fixed metal racking structure typical of a ground-mount HDGI system.
verdicts.rationale: The drawing's own annotation explicitly names an EcoSoch ground-mounted structure, matching the designer's notes.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 layout drawing shows a compass rose (N up, S down, E right, W left) but only gives the site plan orientation, not which way the tilted panel faces are pointed; rows are stacked with a 5m gap label suggesting north-south spacing typical of south-facing rows, but no photo directly shows the panel face direction relative to compass.
verdicts.rationale: The layout hints at a south-facing row arrangement (row spacing to avoid self-shading) but no photo or diagram directly confirms panel face orientation, so this cannot be confirmed visually with confidence.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.designer_notes: Direct walkable access is available to the farmland.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6 and page 7 exterior photos show open, unfenced farmland with no barriers between the approach road and the array area.
verdicts.rationale: The site photos show flat, open, walkable farmland with no obstruction to direct foot access, matching the designer's note.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 'Meter Box' photo shows a single utility pole with a transformer, meter and termination box — this appears to be the site's own low-tension service connection near the road, not a high-tension line running over the PV array; the array itself (pages 6, 9) shows only faint distant poles in the background with no lines crossing directly overhead.
verdicts.rationale: The visible pole/transformer looks like a standard service drop rather than a high-tension transmission line, but exact distance from the array to any line cannot be measured from these photos.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 'Material Delivery Route' photo shows a mud road leading directly to the inverter-room shed, with a hand-drawn route arrow and caption: 'The materials can be delivered to the site via the mud road reaching the inverter room shed allocated for the solar installation.'
verdicts.rationale: The photo and caption directly document a driveable mud road reaching the unloading point, confirming van/truck access.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 7 and 9 show flat open farmland approach with no narrow passages, stairs, or low headroom near the delivery route or array.
verdicts.rationale: No lifting obstacles (stairs, tight corners, overhangs) are visible in any approach or site photo.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: All accessories can be located inside the nearby shed allocated as the inverter room (where a 70 kW battery-based solar inverter and related accessories exists).
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 8 'Material Storage' and page 10 'Equipment Location' photos show the interior of a metal-frame shed already housing existing panel boards/breakers and equipment, with an overlay diagram labeling 'DC-DB', 'INVERTER' and 'AC-DB' positions inside that same shed.
verdicts.rationale: The equipment-location photo explicitly marks DCDB/Inverter/ACDB positions inside the designated shed, matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 'Equipment Location' photo shows the inverter/DCDB/ACDB already positioned inside a fully enclosed, roofed metal shed, sheltered from weather.
verdicts.rationale: Equipment is shown housed inside an enclosed shed, so no separate canopy would be needed, consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_answer: Yes, discussed with the site-in-charge and finalised the location for earthing.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 9 'Cable Routing' photo has an overlay diagram marking specific 'AC Earth Pit' and 'DC Earth Pit' icon locations near the shed, indicating finalized pit placement was documented on site.
verdicts.rationale: The marked earth-pit locations in the site photo overlay support that specific locations were identified/finalized, consistent with the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.designer_answer: The router is available inside the inverter room shed.
verdicts.photo_observation: The 'Equipment Location' photo (page 10) shows the shed interior with DCDB/Inverter/ACDB and misc. tools, but no router or networking device is distinctly visible or labeled in the frame.
verdicts.rationale: No router is visually identifiable in the available shed photos, so this cannot be confirmed even though the shed itself matches.

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: There exists a termination box nearby, which has the parallel connection from the main meter. The cables from the solar meter can be terminated here.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 11 second photo, captioned 'Termination box available nearby with a parallel connection from the main meter', shows an open junction box with red/yellow/blue phase-colored wires terminated on bus bars.
verdicts.rationale: The photo and its caption directly show and describe the termination box referenced in the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Is the Termination Point easily visible or sealed?
verdicts.designer_notes: There exists a termination box nearby, which has the parallel connection from the main meter. The cables from the solar meter can be terminated here.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 11 shows the termination box open with its cover off, phase wires and bus bars clearly exposed and photographed — not sealed.

verdicts.question: Is a Lightning Arrestor (LA) already available at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: The pole in the page 10 'Meter Box' photo carries some overhead hardware near the transformer, but no component is clearly identifiable as a lightning arrestor at the available resolution/angle.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.designer_notes: The solar meter provision has to be fabricated near the termination point located adjacent to the main meter box.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 11 shows the main meter box fully sealed/closed, so its internal space cannot be inspected; the adjacent termination box (also page 11) does appear to have room for new cable entries.
verdicts.rationale: The sealed main meter box prevents any photo-based check of internal spare space, consistent with the designer's own explanation but not independently verifiable.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?
verdicts.designer_notes: The earthing pits can be dug at the space available around the inverter room shed allocated.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 9 'Cable Routing' photo overlay marks 'AC Earth Pit' and 'DC Earth Pit' icon locations in open soil right around the shed, and pages 6/8 show ample open ground surrounding the shed.
verdicts.rationale: Marked pit locations plus visibly open ground around the shed confirm space is available for digging.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: Because of the rough terrain beneath, piling of the footposts can be challenging. However, in order to meet the need, the client is willing to provide support and machinery.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6 and 9 show loose, uneven sandy/rocky soil with sparse scrub across the site, consistent with terrain that could complicate footpost piling.
verdicts.rationale: The visible ground condition (loose sandy/rocky soil) supports the designer's note about challenging terrain for piling.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: All access shown (pages 6, 7) is at ground level across open farmland; there is no elevated roof, ladder, or climbing involved anywhere in the documented photos.
verdicts.rationale: Since the installation is ground-mounted with flat, walkable ground-level access, there is no roof-access safety risk, matching 'No'.

verdicts.question: Should the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB be installed on a metal grill or wall mount?
verdicts.designer_answer: All of the accessories must be installed on a metal grill that will be built within the shed designated for solar power.

verdicts.rationale: A metal frame/grill structure is visibly present inside the shed housing the electrical accessories, matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Is there any trench work to be done to carry the AC cable to the meter location?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: A trench must be excavated in order to carry the DC wires from the intended location to the inverter-room shed.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 CAD layout drawing shows a yellow line explicitly labeled 'Solar DC cable trench' running from the PV array down to the DC-DB/Inverter/AC-DB box location.
verdicts.rationale: The layout drawing documents a planned DC cable trench matching the designer's answer, though the question text itself refers to an AC cable/meter trench while the answer describes a DC trench to the shed — the photographed evidence supports the DC trench as described in the answer.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 shows a proposed 'Solar DC cable trench' line in a CAD drawing (not a photographed cable). Page 9 'Cable Routing' and page 10 'Equipment Location' photos are field/shed photos with color-coded overlay boxes and lines added afterward to indicate planned equipment and pit positions (DC-DB, Inverter, AC-DB, AC/DC Earth Pit) rather than actual installed cables. No physical cable, conduit, or cable-tie is visible running continuously from the PV array to the shed to the meter/termination box (pages 10-11) in any single photo or across photos — the array-to-shed and shed-to-meter connections are only shown as diagrammatic overlays, not as photographed hardware, since this is a pre-installation site visit.
verdicts.rationale: This is a pre-construction TSVR: the documented 'cable routing' consists of proposed/annotated overlay diagrams on site photos rather than actual installed cabling, so physical continuity, conduit, and cable-tie details cannot be traced or verified from the available images.
